findings.reason: The four-step interactive algorithm has a concrete feedback loop whose two uses of the expert are easily conflated: selecting an executed action and labeling all visited states. The original standalone tile contains only prose. A six-stage flow materially clarifies the rollout/label/update separation without altering the algorithm. This is a warranted explanatory addition under the expanded diagram scope, not a failed existing formula.

diagram_math_checks.data: Learner parameter theta_i in K; stationary learner pi_theta_i and deterministic expert pi*:S -> A(s).
diagram_math_checks.check: The learner-to-mixture arrow uses exactly hat pi_i=pi_theta_i. The convex per-decision mixture beta_i pi*+(1-beta_i)hat pi_i is a valid action distribution for beta_i in [0,1], as specified in Definition step 1 and the local imitation-learning definition. The Remarks preserve independent action-selection coins.

diagram_math_checks.data: m trajectories indexed j=1,...,m, each with state times t=0,...,T-1.
diagram_math_checks.check: The mixture-to-rollout arrow executes the selected action; rollout-to-data queries pi*(S_ijt) on every visited state, independently of whether that action was executed. Definition steps 1-2 explicitly distinguish execution from labeling; no arrow sends the saved label back as an automatic rollout action.

This is precisely Definition step 2, with multiplicity retained explicitly in the adjacent prose and uplus notation. S_ijt belongs to S and pi*(S_ijt) belongs to A(S_ijt), so each recorded pair has the required state/action type.

diagram_math_checks.data: Cumulative empirical objective theta -> sum_{r=1}^i Lhat_r(theta), theta in K.
diagram_math_checks.check: Definition step 3 defines Lhat_r as the average of ell(S_rjt,theta) over mT samples. The aggregated labeled blocks retain the states and expert labels of all rounds; the same mT per round means they supply this cumulative objective. The figure does not substitute the population idealization.

diagram_math_checks.data: Supplied deterministic FTL selector and next-round return arrow.
diagram_math_checks.check: Definition step 4 requires attained minimizers and sets theta_{i+1} to that selector’s choice in argmin over K of the cumulative empirical objective. The return arrow advances the learner index only when another training round exists, explicitly stated in Remarks; no extra N+1 rollout is asserted.
